[VLang]: 'mostly a two-state simulator'; === and !== converted to ==/!= when neither side is constant; assigning X gives a constant chosen by --x-assign; setting all variables to one at startup finds the most problems 'since control signals are typically active-high'; the two-state gate primitives (and, buf, nand, nor, not, or, xnor, xor) converted to behavioural equivalents; 'All specify blocks and timing checks are ignored. All min:typ:max delays use the typical value'. All as the document says.

[VArg] imprecision, no change needed to the Knowledge reading: the document says Verilator 'substitutes constants for explicit X values and random constants for initial values, controlled by --x-assign and --x-initial'. On the Arguments page --x-assign defaults to fast (whatever is best for performance, not random), and unique gives a runtime-chosen constant; --x-initial defaults to unique (random) and may be 0 or fast. The document's wording fits the defaults for --x-initial and the unique option for --x-assign; a reader should check the option values used. The repository's own simulation call (eda.py:444) passes neither option, so a repository run uses the defaults.

[OTDV] X-Propagation section: standard RTL simulation ignores the uncertainty of X-valued control signals; gate simulation can detect the problems; Xprop in RTL simulation finds them without gate simulation; optimistic mode 'closer to actual hardware behavior', pessimistic 'more pessimistic than a standard gate-sim'; OpenTitan chooses pessimistic 'as we want to avoid using X value in the condition'. All as the document says. [OTPlan]: tags example 'Run this testpoint in gate level and with power aware. tags: ["gls", "pa"]', as the document says.

[YCell]: the page's flow maps with dfflibmap -liberty and abc -liberty and ends with write_verilog so the file 'can then be loaded into another tool'. [YWV]: -noexpr ('without this option all internal cells are converted to Verilog expressions'), -siminit ('add initial statements with hierarchical refs to initialize FFs when in -noexpr mode'), -norename ('without this option all internal object names ... are changed to short names'). All as the document says. The repository's own synthesis script runs dfflibmap and abc with the Liberty and ends with write_verilog -noattr -noexpr -nohex -nodec (physical.py:170-176), so the repository's netlist keeps internal cells as cells.
